Split lines Product income → Sales of Product Income; Shipping income → Shipping Income; Sales tax collected → Sales Tax Payable; Discounts and refunds → Discounts given; Processing fees → Merchant fees
Split arithmetic: 17,204.11 + 612.00 + 1,489.22 − 503.00 − 369.66 = 18,432.67 — balances to the stated payout total
Account name casing "Merchant fees" and "Discounts given" vs vocabulary.md "Account Names — all words capitalized"; both match real QBO default account names, so not filed

Permanence of the organization-wide mode choice — no text on the screen states the choice is irreversible

findings.element: card: Summary — Downside line, read against the Summary preview split line "Sales tax collected | Sales Tax Payable | 1,489.22"
findings.finding: The only trade-off Summary discloses is the loss of customer and order names, while the preview shows sales tax collapsing into a single undifferentiated Sales Tax Payable journal line with no jurisdiction, so the loss of per-state, filable sales tax detail is never disclosed before an irreversible organization-wide choice.
findings.user_impact: An accountant who picks Summary on this description finds at the first filing deadline that the books carry one lump tax liability with no state breakdown and — because sales tax entered by journal entry does not populate QuickBooks Online's sales tax filing records — cannot produce a per-state return from the books, with no way back short of rebuilding the history.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the tax consequence to the Summary card's disclosed downside in the same plain register as the existing line — for example "Sales tax posts as one total, not per state — file state returns from Synder, not your books" — so both cards state their tax consequence symmetrically before the choice is committed.

evidence.quote: Customer and order names stay in Synder — QuickBooks shows totals only.
evidence.source: Scope: "Missing distinctions" and "Data integrity risks — actions without confirmation that could affect the books irreversibly." Sales tax is a jurisdiction-level statutory liability; a permanent mode choice must disclose that it removes the jurisdiction dimension, and the tooltip on the opposing card already treats "per-state tax" as a decision factor.

findings.element: card: Summary — Benefit line 3 (repeated in the Summary preview note and the Per transaction preview note)
findings.finding: The screen uses "reconciles" for what is actually bank-feed matching; in QuickBooks Online, matching a downloaded deposit to an entry and reconciling an account against a statement are two separate processes, and the entry matching the deposit does not reconcile anything.
findings.user_impact: A bookkeeper reads "reconciles in one click" as the month-end reconciliation being handled by the sync, skips the Reconcile workflow, and closes periods on an account that was never reconciled to a statement — so an unmatched or duplicated payout can sit undetected in the books for months.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the precise accounting terms rather than relabelling to plain language — say the payout entry "matches your bank deposit in one click, so month-end reconciliation clears in one line" and attach a "What's the difference?" tooltip explaining match vs. reconcile, per the rule that compliance-relevant terms stay and are explained, never softened.

evidence.quote: The entry matches your bank deposit exactly, so it reconciles in one click.
evidence.source: Scope: "Incorrect terminology — wrong use of reconciliation." Reconciliation is the periodic agreement of a ledger account to an external statement; matching a bank-feed line to an existing entry is a prerequisite step, not reconciliation.

findings.element: card: Per transaction — Mode name, and card: Summary — Mode name
findings.finding: The two modes are named "Per transaction" and "Summary", but vocabulary.md's canonical product names are "Per Transaction Sync" and "Summary Sync", and the bare word "Summary" additionally collides with Synder's existing Summary objects, which carry their own status vocabulary (Summaries (Transaction), Summaries (Sync)).
findings.user_impact: An accountant running 40+ clients cannot map the permanent setting chosen here onto the product name used in settings, support articles and the "Sync mode changed!" toast, and a bookkeeper reading "Summary" may take it for the Summary record type rather than the organization's posting mode when auditing which client is on which mode.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the canonical names "Per Transaction Sync" and "Summary Sync" as the card titles so the irreversible choice carries the same label as every downstream setting, status and support reference.

evidence.source: vocabulary.md, "Synder Product Names": **Per Transaction Sync**, **Summary Sync** — and "Statuses → Summaries (Transaction)" / "Summaries (Sync)", which already reserve "Summary" for a different object.

gaps: Preview modal / Per transaction: the state map lists "Real QuickBooks output" as not exercised — "the register shown is authored sample data, not a live sync; its accuracy against production is unverified" — so I cannot confirm the posting shape. The supplied production QuickBooks Online reference shows sales arriving as Payment / Invoice pairs (an Accounts Receivable path, statuses Closed / Paid), while the preview shows Sales Receipt rows (no A/R). One of the two is wrong for this integration and the state map cannot settle which.

Preview modal / Per transaction: the Account column shows only income and expense accounts (Shopify Sales, Shopify Refunds, Merchant fees) and never the account the cash lands in, so whether 412 sales receipts post to a clearing / Undeposited Funds account or directly to the bank is unrecorded. This matters because the note claims "Reconciling the bank deposit means matching 412 entries to one deposit line" — in QuickBooks Online individual receipts must first be grouped into a bank deposit before a single deposit line can be matched, so the described workflow may not be reproducible.

Preview modal: the prototype's columns are Date | Entry | Account | Amount, while the production reference's Sales transactions list is Date | Type | No. | Customer | Memo | Amount | Status | Action. "Entry" is not a QuickBooks Online column name and no Status column appears, so whether the preview is meant to depict the Sales transactions list or an account register is not recorded, and I cannot judge fidelity against the reference on that basis alone.

Commit path: "What happens after the choice is saved" is listed as not exercised ("no backend in the prototype; the confirmation and first-sync behaviour cannot be observed here"), so whether this permanent, organization-wide setting is guarded by a confirmation step — vocabulary.md's "Are you sure you want to proceed?" pattern — is unknown. An irreversible book-affecting choice with no observed confirmation is the exact data-integrity risk my lens exists to catch, and I cannot clear or flag it from the map.

Whole screen: nothing in the state map states on screen that the choice is permanent, even though the primary task says it is. Whether that warning appears at the Continue step cannot be checked, since "Continue / Back buttons" are listed as not exercised ("prototype has no next or previous step wired").

Multi-client scope: the state map does not record whether the sync mode binds to the organization, to the accounting company, or to each Shopify integration. A firm connecting a second Shopify store for the same client cannot tell from this screen whether it inherits the mode, and I cannot determine it from the map.
